steps.decide: Whether the message is a toast at all, or belongs inline next to what it describes
Politeness, and whether the message may disappear on its own
Placement that does not cover the control the user is using
Entry and exit motion and the reduced-motion equivalent

rules.statement: Toasts carry transient confirmation or a repairable warning; anything the user must act on belongs inline or in a dialog.
Toasts are announced through a polite live region and error toasts through an assertive one; neither steals focus.
An error toast does not auto-dismiss; a confirmation may, after a duration long enough to read it twice.
Toasts never cover the primary action or the focused control, and they do not stack beyond three.
Reduced motion removes the slide but keeps position, duration and the live-region announcement.

motion.reducedMotion: appears instantly in place, announcement unchanged
appears instantly and does not auto-dismiss

motion.noneReason: hover only pauses the timer; the toast does not move

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a toast for a superseded action is dropped rather than shown late

refused.reason: a confirmation variant cannot report a failure
an error variant cannot confirm success

sections.intent: Confirm or warn about something transient without taking over the screen.
nicheDifferences: Operate toasts must not obscure a control mid-task
Commerce confirmations need a route to the cart
a11y: Polite live region for confirmations, assertive for errors
responsive: Full width at 390px with safe-area insets
copy: States the outcome, not the mechanism
No error toast without a retry path
alternatives: Inline status beneath the control is preferable when context matters
A dialog is required when the user must decide
